lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Priya, it's Luis from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about my blood work.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That Coke is part of your routine, and giving it up feels like losing something.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, it was a long weekend with family, you know how it is. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really like my Coke with lunch. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I can do water at lunch, maybe not dinner yet. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I swap soda for water on 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 4 out of 4 days, the hard part was the late dinners, and next week you're going to swap soda for water on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

Daughter support question; answer is no
Water does not satisfy; reason against change
Directive priority statement; no permission asked
Feels better about self when sticking to it
Wants to act to avoid cancer returning
Will swap water at lunch; easier now
Goal: water for soda on 5 days
Plans bigger lunch to manage barrier
Summary wrongly says 4 of 4 days this week

flags.reason: Warns about health consequences without asking permission; pushes rather than eliciting the participant's own reasons.
'You have to make this a priority' is directive and creates resistance; participant responded with sustain talk.
Says participant did soda swap 4 of 4 days this week, which the participant never reported; misrepresents progress.
Participant's blood work question was never acknowledged or answered; coach redirected to agenda at line 5.

score.summary: Luis got to a concrete goal (water for soda on 5 days, confidence 9/10) and planned for the late-dinner barrier, which is a solid structure. However, he twice used directive persuasion ('You have to make this a priority'), ignored Priya's blood work question, and misstated her progress in the summary.
strengths: Line 16 reflected the emotional weight of giving up Coke ('giving it up feels like losing something'), which helped Priya keep talking.
Line 36 used a 0-10 confidence scale and line 38 asked about barriers, building a realistic plan.
Line 29 affirmed Priya for identifying her own reason to change ('You figured that out on your own').
coaching_tips: Line 10 and line 19 moved into persuading; replace with 'Would it be OK if I shared what I've seen work for others?' or reflect the ambivalence instead.
Line 4: acknowledge the blood work question briefly and schedule time or note it for follow-up before moving to the agenda.
Line 40: check summaries against what the participant actually reported; the 4-of-4 claim was not stated and should be corrected.
Line 21 asked about good days well; follow up on that answer more with open questions rather than moving quickly to a goal.
